Manx: My Charrey deyr mainshter Wood, ta me [mee] booisal dhiu erson ny screenyn [screeunyn] gaelkagh [Gailckagh] ta shiu cha mie dy cur dou as yn lioar leideilys [leeideilys]  mannin-aght [Manninagh].
English: My dear friend Mister Wood, I am grateful to you for the Manx letters you are so good to send to me and the Manx guidance book.

Manx: T’ee cur lane taitnys dow dy lhaih ee, shoilshaghey [soilshaghey] ymmodee reddin [reddyn] nagh vell [vel] re-gheddyn [ry-gheddyn]  ayns lioar erbee elley.
English: It gives me great pleasure to read it, explaining many things that aren’t to be found in any other book.

Manx: T’eh cur lane taitnys dooin dy clashtyn dy vel ben ainsher Wood gheddyn ny share,
English: It gives me a lot of pleasure to hear that Mrs Wood is getting better,

Manx: ta’n ven ayms er veh [ve] cummal eh lhiabbee rish kegeeish agh t’ee gheddin ny share.
English: My wife has been keeping to her bed for a fortnight, but she is getting better.

Manx: Ta shin yeearree shiu blein vie noa as ymmodee imbaghyn maynrey cooidjagh.
English: We wish you a good new year and many happy season together.
